facts.text: Mill Woods was Edmonton’s first socially planned community, built on city‑owned land to foster a strong sense of neighborhood.
The original plan featured a town centre and eight surrounding communities, each split into multiple neighbourhoods with crescent‑shaped streets.
Mixed housing in Mill Woods blends single‑family homes, high‑rise apartments, and co‑operatives, creating a diverse urban landscape.
Indigenous peoples, Canadian migrants, and immigrants from South Asia, East Africa, the Philippines, the Caribbean, and Latin America have shaped Mill Woods’ cultural mosaic.
Annual celebrations in Mill Woods include a Sikh parade, Caribbean “Mas Camps,” and Spanish‑language community dances on Canada Day.
Mill Woods Christian School, founded in 1978 in the Tweddle Place neighbourhood, became an alternative program of the Edmonton Public School Board in 2000.
